model_interpretation.claim: Packing short H rows into each CTA should reduce CTA overhead and inactive threads in the separate forward and input-gradient passes. The mapping uses row_width=min(L,256) and packs floor(256/row_width) rows per CTA; for L=48, this assigns five rows to a 240-thread CTA instead of launching one 256-thread CTA per row. Rows of length at least 256 retain the existing one-row, 256-thread mapping. The baseline is correct at 35.464 ms mean for the full call, but it does not isolate these kernels; any benefit remains unmeasured.

items.subject: Improve forward and input-gradient CTA mapping without fusion
items.objective: Own the separate forward and input-gradient kernels and their launch mapping in src/candidate.cu. Explore packing multiple short rows per CTA and other coalesced, well-utilized mappings to reduce inactive threads and CTA overhead; keep the two passes separate so this tree isolates mapping/kernel-efficiency gains from fusion. Preserve bounds-safe zero padding, full FP32, all-input correctness, complete output writes, and the fixed API. Judge candidates by correctness and full-call timing, not an assumed per-kernel benefit.
